title: Block32-causal attention, six schedules
formula: out = softmax(mask(Q @ K^T / sqrt(128))) @ V with mask key // 32 <= query // 32, top-left aligned; FP16 [BH*S, 128] Q/K/V and FP16 probabilities, FP32 out plus FP32 rowmax and rowsum
study_for: Six schedules, one algorithm, one file. v1 is a two-slot lag-1 partition, v2 adds a next-query prefetch with independent producer and consumer counters, v3 deepens the lag to three over a four-slot snake, v4 batches four key tiles into a group, v5 adds an eight-tile V preload ring, v6 flattens each core's (m_tile, group) work into one continuous stream so the pipeline fills once at the start instead of once per M tile. Every case names a variant and changes nothing else, so the six are directly comparable on the same four shapes.

The constants that are not shared are the point of merging the six into one file. All six define TILE_M/TILE_N/BLOCK_CAUSAL identically, and all six share every masking helper (`build_suffix_invalid_mask`, `apply_diagonal_tile_block32_causal_mask` and the rest) byte for byte -- so those appear once. What does not de-duplicate is v4's lookahead-two/four-slot ring against v5 and v6's lookahead-three/five-slot ring, kept apart here as `V4_GROUP_LOOKAHEAD`/`V4_GROUP_STAGE_SLOTS` versus `GROUP_LOOKAHEAD`/`GROUP_STAGE_SLOTS`. Six separate modules hid that difference behind one name.

Why every variant has a `ring_wrap` case at 769 tokens. The workspace rings are GMBuffs: the producer writes slot `g % SLOTS` while the consumer reads slot `(g - LOOKAHEAD) % SLOTS`, so the ring must be strictly larger than the lookahead or the two alias. A shape small enough to never wrap proves nothing about that invariant, and both simulators model the slot reuse and the mutex depth that enforce it.

Three outputs, and the row statistics are the diagnostic. `rowmax` and `rowsum` are the FP32 state captured before the probabilities are rounded to FP16, so main.py holds them to 1e-05 while `out` gets 0.005 -- if `out` is wrong and the statistics are right, the fault is in PV, not in the softmax. They are published per head at a stride padded to a multiple of eight FP32 values so two heads never share a 32-byte GM line, and `execute` slices that padding off on the host rather than in the kernel.
do_not_copy_when: Your causal mask is per token. This is a block staircase at BLOCK_CAUSAL = 32: every query in a 32-token block sees exactly the same key prefix, which is what lets whole diagonal tiles be masked with one helper instead of row by row.

Your head dimension is not 128, or your tiles are not 128x128. TILE_M/TILE_N/TILE_K and the half-tile vector sub-blocks are all that number, and the L1/L0C budgets of all six schedules were sized against it.

You want the simplest possible starting point. v1 is the one to read first and the other five are variations on it -- start anywhere else and you will be reading pipeline bookkeeping before you have read the algorithm.
Your S2 is below 64 and you want v5 or v6. Their disjoint V backfill reads 128 - valid_n rows from the head of the tensor, and shorter sequences do not have those rows to read.
